You are reviewing a Python stdlib tool `stockroom` in /tmp/hzt-3388928427/bench-run-syikcu3b/clone/.harness/worktrees/orch-VocanicZ_bench-run-20261115-medium-harness-opus-harness-opus-r03-p1 (work only there; do not modify tracked files — use scratch dirs under /tmp/stockroom-probe-$$ for test data). The spec is brief.md in that dir (top authority) plus PRD #1 (`gh issue view 1 -R VocanicZ/bench-run-20261115-medium-harness-opus-harness-opus-r03`, read its "Implementation Decisions" and "Acceptance criteria"). Code in src/stockroom/, tests in tests/. Run the CLI via `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m stockroom ...`.

Tasks:
1. Check EVERY acceptance criterion against the code and actual behaviour; report met/unmet per criterion with evidence. Look hard at correctness: pricing steps 1-6 (half-up rounding, largest-remainder allocation with ties to earlier line, tax per line), negative-stock detection in date order, fulfil availability with later movements, shipped quantity rules, report sort/format, exit codes (2 for cmdline errors checked before reading files, 1 for data errors with stdout empty), file reading per command, receive/ship byte-identical refusal and newline-add, --dir anywhere, options spelled in full (no abbreviations), brief's worked stock/quote examples reproduce exactly.
2. Run this robustness probe against the real CLI and report EACH result pass/fail with the exact command:
   - a value starting with a dash, positional and as option value: e.g. `history -x`, `quote -`, `--dir -x`, `--dir --json`, `--format -`, `receive 2024-03-10 AB-100 -5`, `receive 2024-03-10 AB-100 5 -note`, `receive 2024-03-10 AB-100 5 --json`, `history --`.
   - output piped into `head -1` (stock, history, report, quote): no traceback, exit 0 (check with PIPESTATUS); also with a large catalogue (e.g. 20000 products) so the pipe really closes mid-write.
   - UTF-8 BOM at start of each of the three files.
   - CRLF and lone-CR line endings in each file (lone CR must not split lines; check what error/behaviour results).
   - form feed U+000C and U+2028 inside a field (name, note, customer) — should not split lines; check whether whitespace-trimming treats them as whitespace (PRD says only space/tab are whitespace) and how output renders.
   - non-UTF-8 bytes in each file -> exit 2; missing dir -> exit 2; directory named catalog.txt; empty files.
   - library: ParseError attributes, types of returned fields, `price_order` with an object having .lines.
3. Report concise findings: list each unmet criterion and each user-visible I/O issue (args, parsing, output format, exit code, error message, encodings, line endings, closed pipe) as separate numbered items with repro command, expected vs actual. Be terse. Don't pad with things that pass beyond a one-line pass list.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. # Stockroom

I run a small online shop out of a spare room and I keep everything in plain text files: what I sell,
what came in and went out of the shelves, and what customers ordered. I'd like a Python tool called
**stockroom** that reads those files and answers three questions: what is on the shelves and what
needs buying, what an order costs, and what I can ship today. It should work two ways: as a library I
can `import stockroom` from my own scripts, and as a `stockroom` command in the terminal. Python 3.9 or
newer, standard library only (no third-party packages). Running `pip install .` in the project folder
should give me both the importable library and the `stockroom` command.

There are two halves to it: the **shelves** (the catalogue, the stock movements, what is low) and the
**orders** (prices, discounts, tax, shipping what is in stock, invoices, a report). The orders half
depends on the shelves, so build them in that order.

## The three files

They live in one folder (the command's current folder, or the one named by `--dir`). Text is UTF-8; a
byte order mark at the start of a file is ignored; a line ends at LF or at CRLF and nowhere else.
In every file, blank lines are ignored, and so are lines starting with `#` (after any leading
whitespace). Anything else that does not follow the rules below is a mistake in my file, and the tool
must tell me which file and which line (counting from 1, blank and comment lines included).

### `catalog.txt` — what I sell

One product per line, fields separated by `|`, whitespace around each field trimmed:

```
# SKU   | name            | price | reorder | tax
AB-100 | Garden gnome     | 12.50 | 5       | standard
cd-205 | Seed packet, mix | 1.99  | 40      | reduced
EF-310 | Gift voucher     | 25.00 | 0
```

- **SKU**: two to four letters, a dash, three digits (`AB-100`). Letters in any case are accepted; the
  SKU is always shown in upper case. Two lines with the same SKU are a mistake.
- **name**: not empty. It may contain anything except `|`.
- **price**: in pounds, at least `0.01`, at most two decimal places (`12`, `12.5`, `1.99` are fine;
  `12.505`, `1,000.00`, `-3` and `abc` are not).
- **reorder**: the stock level at or under which I need to buy more: a whole number, zero or more.
- **tax** (optional, `standard` when the field is left out, so a line has four or five fields): one of
  `standard` (20 %), `reduced` (5 %) or `zero` (0 %), in any case.

### `movements.txt` — what came in and went out

One movement per line: `DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]`, separated by any amount of spaces or tabs. The note
is the rest of the line exactly as written, apart from trimming whitespace at both ends.

```
2024-03-01 AB-100 +20 first delivery
2024-03-04 ab-100 -3 order SO-1001
2024-03-05 CD-205 40
```

- **DATE** is `YYYY-MM-DD` and a date that exists (`2024-02-30` is a mistake).
- **SKU** must be in the catalogue (any case).
- **QUANTITY** is a whole number that is not zero, with an optional sign: positive means stock in,
  negative means stock out.
- The movements count in date order; movements on the same day keep the order of the file. The
  stock of a product may never be below zero at any point in that order. The line that takes it below
  zero is the mistake.

### `orders.txt` — what customers ordered

One order per line: `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER LINES`, separated by any amount of spaces or tabs:

```
SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme AB-100*12,CD-205*3
SO-1002 2024-03-09 Bea ab-100*2
```

- **ORDER** is `SO-` (any case) and one or more digits, shown in upper case; `SO-7` and `SO-007` are two
  different orders. It is unique: a second line with the same order number is a mistake.
- **DATE** as above. **CUSTOMER** is one word, shown as typed.
- **LINES** is one or more `SKU*QUANTITY` pairs separated by commas, no spaces. The SKU must be in the
  catalogue and appear once per order; the quantity is a whole number of one or more (no sign).

A missing `catalog.txt` is an error for every command. A missing `movements.txt` or `orders.txt` is
just empty. A command reads only the files it needs, and a mistake in a file it does not read is not its
business: the shelves commands (`stock`, `low`, `history`, `receive`, `ship`) read the catalogue and the
movements; `quote` reads the catalogue and the orders; `fulfil`, `invoice` and `report` read all three.

## Using it as a library

```python
import stockroom

catalog = stockroom.parse_catalog(open("catalog.txt").read())
moves = stockroom.parse_movements(open("movements.txt").read(), catalog)
print(stockroom.stock_levels(catalog, moves))
```

- `parse_catalog(text)` returns a `dict` of SKU to a product. A product has `.sku`, `.name`, `.price`
  (a `decimal.Decimal`), `.reorder` (an `int`) and `.tax` (`"standard"`, `"reduced"` or `"zero"`).
- `parse_movements(text, catalog)` returns a list of movements in the order they appear in the text,

# Stockroom

I run a small online shop out of a spare room and I keep everything in plain text files: what I sell,
what came in and went out of the shelves, and what customers ordered. I'd like a Python tool called

can `import stockroom` from my own scripts, and as a `stockroom` command in the terminal. Python 3.9 or
newer, standard library only (no third-party packages). Running `pip install .` in the project folder
should give me both the importable library and the `stockroom` command.

There are two halves to it: the **shelves** (the catalogue, the stock movements, what is low) and the
**orders** (prices, discounts, tax, shipping what is in stock, invoices, a report). The orders half
depends on the shelves, so build them in that order.

They live in one folder (the command's current folder, or the one named by `--dir`). Text is UTF-8; a
byte order mark at the start of a file is ignored; a line ends at LF or at CRLF and nowhere else.
In every file, blank lines are ignored, and so are lines starting with `#` (after any leading
whitespace). Anything else that does not follow the rules below is a mistake in my file, and the tool
must tell me which file and which line (counting from 1, blank and comment lines included).

### `catalog.txt` — what I sell

One product per line, fields separated by `|`, whitespace around each field trimmed:

```
# SKU   | name            | price | reorder | tax
AB-100 | Garden gnome     | 12.50 | 5       | standard
cd-205 | Seed packet, mix | 1.99  | 40      | reduced
EF-310 | Gift voucher     | 25.00 | 0
```

  SKU is always shown in upper case. Two lines with the same SKU are a mistake.
- **name**: not empty. It may contain anything except `|`.
- **price**: in pounds, at least `0.01`, at most two decimal places (`12`, `12.5`, `1.99` are fine;
  `12.505`, `1,000.00`, `-3` and `abc` are not).
- **reorder**: the stock level at or under which I need to buy more: a whole number, zero or more.
- **tax** (optional, `standard` when the field is left out, so a line has four or five fields): one of
  `standard` (20 %), `reduced` (5 %) or `zero` (0 %), in any case.

2024-03-04 ab-100 -3 order SO-1001
2024-03-05 CD-205 40

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

schema.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

content.content:
# Stockroom

I run a small online shop out of a spare room and I keep everything in plain text files: what I sell,
what came in and went out of the shelves, and what customers ordered. I'd like a Python tool called
**stockroom** that reads those files and answers three questions: what is on the shelves and what
needs buying, what an order costs, and what I can ship today. It should work two ways: as a library I
can `import stockroom` from my own scripts, and as a `stockroom` command in the terminal. Python 3.9 or
newer, standard library only (no third-party packages). Running `pip install .` in the project folder
should give me both the importable library and the `stockroom` command.

There are two halves to it: the **shelves** (the catalogue, the stock movements, what is low) and the
**orders** (prices, discounts, tax, shipping what is in stock, invoices, a report). The orders half
depends on the shelves, so build them in that order.

## The three files

They live in one folder (the command's current folder, or the one named by `--dir`). Text is UTF-8; a
byte order mark at the start of a file is ignored; a line ends at LF or at CRLF and nowhere else.
In every file, blank lines are ignored, and so are lines starting with `#` (after any leading
whitespace). Anything else that does not follow the rules below is a mistake in my file, and the tool
must tell me which file and which line (counting from 1, blank and comment lines included).

### `catalog.txt` — what I sell

One product per line, fields separated by `|`, whitespace around each field trimmed:

```
# SKU   | name            | price | reorder | tax
AB-100 | Garden gnome     | 12.50 | 5       | standard
cd-205 | Seed packet, mix | 1.99  | 40      | reduced
EF-310 | Gift voucher     | 25.00 | 0
```

- **SKU**: two to four letters, a dash, three digits (`AB-100`). Letters in any case are accepted; the
  SKU is always shown in upper case. Two lines with the same SKU are a mistake.
- **name**: not empty. It may contain anything except `|`.
- **price**: in pounds, at least `0.01`, at most two decimal places (`12`, `12.5`, `1.99` are fine;
  `12.505`, `1,000.00`, `-3` and `abc` are not).
- **reorder**: the stock level at or under which I need to buy more: a whole number, zero or more.
- **tax** (optional, `standard` when the field is left out, so a line has four or five fields): one of
  `standard` (20 %), `reduced` (5 %) or `zero` (0 %), in any case.

### `movements.txt` — what came in and went out

One movement per line: `DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]`, separated by any amount of spaces or tabs. The note
is the rest of the line exactly as written, apart from trimming whitespace at both ends.

```
2024-03-01 AB-100 +20 first delivery
2024-03-04 ab-100 -3 order SO-1001
2024-03-05 CD-205 40
```

- **DATE** is `YYYY-MM-DD` and a date that exists (`2024-02-30` is a mistake).
- **SKU** must be in the catalogue (any case).
- **QUANTITY** is a whole number that is not zero, with an optional sign: positive means stock in,
  negative means stock out.
- The movements count in date order; movements on the same day keep the order of the file. The
  stock of a product may never be below zero at any point in that order. The line that takes it below
  zero is the mistake.

### `orders.txt` — what customers ordered

One order per line: `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER LINES`, separated by any amount of spaces or tabs:

```
SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme AB-100*12,CD-205*3
SO-1002 2024-03-09 Bea ab-100*2
```

- **ORDER** is `SO-` (any case) and one or more digits, shown in upper case; `SO-7` and `SO-007` are two
  different orders. It is unique: a second line with the same order number is a mistake.
- **DATE** as above. **CUSTOMER** is one word, shown as typed.
- **LINES** is one or more `SKU*QUANTITY` pairs separated by commas, no spaces. The SKU must be in the
  catalogue and appear once per order; the quantity is a whole number of one or more (no sign).

A missing `catalog.txt` is an error for every command. A missing `movements.txt` or `orders.txt` is
just empty. A command reads only the files it needs, and a mistake in a file it does not read is not its
business: the shelves commands (`stock`, `low`, `history`, `receive`, `ship`) read the catalogue and the
movements; `quote` reads the catalogue and the orders; `fulfil`, `invoice` and `report` read all three.

## Using it as a library

```python
import stockroom

catalog = stockroom.parse_catalog(open("catalog.txt").read())
moves = stockroom.parse_movements(open("movements.txt").read(), catalog)
print(stockroom.stock_levels(catalog, moves))
```

- `parse_catalog(text)` returns a `dict` of SKU to a product. A product has `.sku`, `.name`, `.price`
  (a `decimal.Decimal`), `.reorder` (an `int`) and `.tax` (`"standard"`, `"reduced"` or `"zero"`).
- `parse_movements(text, catalog)` returns a list of movements in the order they appear in the text,
  each with `.date` (a `datetime.date`), `.sku`, `.quantity` (an `int`) and `.note` (a `str`, empty when
  there is none).
- `parse_orders(text, catalog)` returns a list of orders in the order they appear, each with `.id`,
  `.date`, `.customer` and `.lines`: a list of `(sku, quantity)` pairs in the order written.
- A bad line makes any of these raise `stockroom.ParseError`. It is a `ValueError`, its `.line`
  attribute is the line number, and its message mentions `line N`.
- `stock_levels(catalog, movements)` is a `dict` of SKU to the quantity on the shelf, for every product
  in the catalogue (zero when it never moved).
- `price_order(order, catalog)` prices a whole order as described under *Prices* and returns a quote with
  `.lines` (each with `.sku`, `.quantity`, `.unit`, `.gross`, `.discount`, `.net`), `.subtotal`,
  `.order_discount`, `.tax` and `.total`, all `Decimal`s with two decimal places. A discount is zero or
  negative.

## Prices

All of this is exact to the penny and every rounding step rounds halves **up** (`0.005` becomes `0.01`).

1. A line's **gross** is its quantity times the unit price.
2. A line gets a **volume discount** of 5 % of its gross when the quantity is 10 or more, and 10 % when it
   is 50 or more (not both), rounded to the penny. The line's **net** is gross minus that.
3. The **subtotal** is the sum of the nets. When it is £500.00 or more the whole order gets an **order
   discount** of 3 % of the subtotal, rounded to the penny.
4. The order discount is shared out over the lines in proportion to their nets, to the penny: each line's
   share is rounded down, and the pennies left over go one each to the lines with the biggest part of a
   penny lost (the earlier line first on a tie). A line's **taxable amount** is its net less its share.
5. **Tax** is worked out per line on its taxable amount at its product's rate, rounded to the penny, and
   added up. Prices do not include tax.
6. The **total** is the subtotal, plus the order discount (a negative number), plus the tax.

## Using it from the terminal

Every command takes `--dir DIR` anywhere on the line (default: the current folder). Options are spelled out in full.

```
$ stockroom stock
AB-100 17 ok Garden gnome
CD-205 40 low Seed packet, mix
EF-310 0 out Gift voucher

$ stockroom quote SO-1001
SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme
AB-100 12 12.50 150.00 -7.50 142.50
CD-205 3 1.99 5.97 0.00 5.97
subtotal 148.47
order discount 0.00
tax 28.80
total 177.27
```

**The shelves**

- `stockroom stock [--json]` prints one line per product, by SKU: `SKU ONHAND STATUS NAME` separated by single
  spaces. The status is `out` when the stock is zero, `low` when it is above zero and at or under the product's
  reorder level, `ok` otherwise.
- `stockroom low [--json]` prints one line for each product that is `low` or `out`, by SKU:
  `SKU ONHAND REORDER BUY` where BUY is how many to buy to get back to twice the reorder level, and at least 1
  (`max(1, 2 × reorder − onhand)`).
- `stockroom history SKU [--json]` prints that product's movements, in the order they count, one per
  line as `DATE DELTA BALANCE NOTE`: the quantity with its sign (`+20`, `-3`), the stock after the
  movement, and the note (and its space) left out when there is none. A SKU that is not in the catalogue is
  refused.
- `stockroom receive DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` and `stockroom ship DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` add a stock-in or
  stock-out movement to the end of `movements.txt` (creating it if needed) and print the line they added,
  written the way `history` writes a movement without the balance: `DATE SKU ±QUANTITY NOTE`. The quantity is a
  whole number of one or more, no sign. I pass the note as a single quoted argument; a note may not contain a
  line break. A movement that would break a rule above (an unknown SKU, a quantity that is not a positive
  whole number, stock that would go below zero at any point in date order) is refused and the file is left
  exactly as it was. If the file does not end in a newline, one is added before the new line.

**The orders**

- `stockroom quote ORDER [--json]` prints the order priced as in the example: a header line
  `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER`, one line per order line `SKU QUANTITY UNIT GROSS DISCOUNT NET`, then
  `subtotal`, `order discount`, `tax` and `total` lines. Amounts have two decimals, discounts carry a minus
  sign (zero has none), values are separated by single spaces. An order that is not in `orders.txt` is
  refused.
- `stockroom fulfil ORDER DATE` ships what the shelves can cover. For each order line, what is still owed is its
  quantity less what earlier shipments of this order sent (the total of the negative quantities for that SKU in movements
  whose note is exactly `order SO-1001`, the order number in upper case; capped at the quantity ordered). It ships as many of those as the shelves allow on
  DATE: no more than the stock after all movements dated on or before DATE, and no more than the lowest stock at
  any later point (so that the shipment never makes a later movement take the stock below zero). It adds one
  movement `DATE SKU -N order SO-1001` per line with something to ship, at the end of the file. It prints one
  line per order line, `SKU shipped N backordered M` (M is what is still owed afterwards), then
  `status open`, `status partial` or `status complete`: `complete` when nothing is owed on any line, `open` when
  nothing has been shipped on any line yet, `partial` otherwise. DATE may not be before the order's date
  (refused).
- `stockroom invoice ORDER [--json]` is `quote` for what has actually shipped: the same rules and the same
  layout, with the quantities shipped so far (lines with nothing shipped are left out) and `invoice ` in front
  of the header line (`invoice SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme`). An order with nothing shipped is refused.
- `stockroom report [--format text|csv|json]` has one row per order, by order date and then by order
  number: `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER STATUS SHIPPED/ORDERED QUOTED INVOICED`: the status as above, the units shipped and
  ordered, the quote's total, and the invoice's total (`0.00` when nothing has shipped). `text` is the
  default and separates by single spaces. `csv` has the header
  `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`; `json` is an array of objects with those keys,
  the units as numbers and the amounts as strings with two decimals.
- With `--json`, `stock` prints an array of `{"sku", "name", "onhand", "status"}`, `low` an array of
  `{"sku", "onhand", "reorder", "buy"}`, `history` an array of `{"date", "delta", "balance", "note"}`, and
  `quote` / `invoice` an object with `order`, `date`, `customer`, `lines` (objects with `sku`, `quantity`,
  `unit`, `gross`, `discount`, `net`), `subtotal`, `order_discount`, `tax` and `total`. Amounts are strings
  with two decimals, counts are numbers, except a history `delta`, which is the signed string (`"+20"`, `"-3"`).
- `receive`, `ship` and `fulfil` take no options except `--dir`: every other argument is taken as typed, so a
  dash-led quantity is a bad quantity (refused) and a dash-led note is a note.
- The command line is checked first (exit `2` for anything wrong with it), then the files are read, then the
  request is carried out.
- Exit status: `0` when it worked; `1` when a data file has a mistake or what I asked for is refused (an unknown
  SKU or order, a movement that would break a rule, nothing shipped yet), with a message on standard error that
  names the file and the line where there is one, and nothing on standard output; `2` when a file cannot be read
  (a missing `catalog.txt`, a folder that does not exist, bytes that are not UTF-8) or the command line is wrong
  (no command, an unknown command, the wrong number of arguments, an unknown option, a bad option value, a date I
  mistyped).
- If whatever is reading the output goes away (`stockroom stock | head -1`) it just stops quietly, with status
  `0`.

## Implementation Decisions

**Layout.** `pyproject.toml` (setuptools backend, `requires-python = ">=3.9"`, no dependencies, `[project.scripts] stockroom = "stockroom.cli:main"`), package in `src/stockroom/` (suggested modules: `parsing.py`/`models.py` for shelves, `pricing.py`, `cli.py`, `__main__.py` so `python -m stockroom` works). `__init__.py` re-exports `ParseError, parse_catalog, parse_movements, parse_orders, stock_levels, price_order` and the record types. Records are frozen dataclasses (`Product`, `Movement`, `Order`, `QuoteLine`, `Quote`).

**Text handling (all three files, library and CLI alike).**
- A leading U+FEFF is dropped. Lines are split on `\n` only; one trailing `\r` before the `\n` is removed. Never use `str.splitlines()` (it splits on `\r`, `\x0b`, `\x1c`, U+2028, …). A lone `\r` elsewhere stays part of the line.
- "Whitespace" for trimming and for separators means space and tab only. A blank line = only spaces/tabs. A comment line = first non-space/tab char is `#`.
- Line numbers count every physical line from 1, including blank and comment lines.
- `ParseError(ValueError)` has `.line` (int) and a message containing `line N`. The CLI prefixes the file name: `stockroom: catalog.txt: line 3: bad price '12.505'`.

**Field rules.**
- SKU: regex `[A-Za-z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3}` (full match, ASCII only), stored upper-case. Duplicate SKU (case-insensitive) in the catalogue is a mistake on the second line.
- Catalogue: split on `|`, trim each field; exactly 4 or 5 fields; empty name is a mistake; price matches `[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,2})?` and is >= 0.01 (stored as `Decimal`, quantized to 2 places is fine); reorder matches `[0-9]+`; tax case-insensitive in {standard, reduced, zero}, stored lower-case; an empty 5th field is a mistake.
- Dates: `[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}` and a valid calendar date.
- Movement line: split on runs of spaces/tabs into at most 4 parts (date, sku, qty, rest); note = rest trimmed of space/tab, `""` when absent. Quantity matches `[+-]?[0-9]+` and is non-zero. SKU must be in the catalogue. `parse_movements` itself checks that stock never goes below zero, processing movements in date order (stable sort, file order within a day); the first line (in that order) that takes a stock below zero raises ParseError with that line's number.
- Order line: exactly 4 space/tab separated fields. Id matches `[Ss][Oo]-[0-9]+`, stored upper-case, leading zeros kept (`SO-7` != `SO-007`); duplicates are a mistake. Customer kept as typed. Lines: split on `,`; each part must full-match `SKU\*[0-9]+` with quantity >= 1; an empty part (e.g. trailing comma) is a mistake; SKU in catalogue, not repeated within the order.

**Pricing.** `Decimal` throughout, `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `0.01` at each step, exactly per the brief's steps 1-6. Volume discount 10 % at qty >= 50, else 5 % at qty >= 10. Order discount 3 % of subtotal when subtotal >= 500.00. Allocation: exact share = D * net_i / subtotal (in pennies), floor each, distribute leftover pennies by largest fractional remainder, ties to the earlier line. Tax rates standard 0.20, reduced 0.05, zero 0. Discounts are returned as zero or negative (`Decimal("0.00")`, not `-0.00`). `price_order(order, catalog)` works on any object with `.lines` of `(sku, qty)` — invoice reuses it with shipped quantities.

**Shipped quantities (fulfil / invoice / report).** For order X and SKU S: shipped = min(ordered qty, sum of `-quantity` over movements with `quantity < 0`, `sku == S` and note exactly `order X` (X upper-case)). Status: `complete` if nothing owed on any line, `open` if shipped is 0 on every line, else `partial`.

**fulfil availability.** For a SKU, with movements in counting order: available = min(balance after all movements dated <= DATE, every balance after each later-dated movement); ship n = min(owed, max(0, available)). One appended movement `DATE SKU -n order X` per line with n > 0, in order-line order. Prints `SKU shipped n backordered m` per order line (including n = 0) then `status …` computed after the shipment. If nothing can be shipped, nothing is written and exit is 0.

**CLI.** Hand-written argument handling (not argparse's abbreviation behaviour): `--dir DIR` and `--dir=DIR` accepted anywhere; options must be spelled in full. `--json` for stock/low/history/quote/invoice; `--format text|csv|json` (or `--format=…`) for report. For `receive`, `ship`, `fulfil` only `--dir` is recognised; every other argument is positional, taken as typed. `receive`/`ship` take 3 or 4 positionals (DATE SKU QTY [NOTE]); `fulfil` exactly 2; `history`, `quote`, `invoice` exactly 1; `stock`, `low`, `report` 0.
- Exit 2 (checked before reading any file): no command, unknown command, wrong positional count, unknown option, option missing its value, bad `--format` value, a malformed or non-existent DATE argument (receive/ship/fulfil). Also exit 2: `--dir` folder does not exist, `catalog.txt` missing, any needed file not valid UTF-8 or otherwise unreadable.
- Exit 1: a mistake in a file the command reads (only the files listed in the brief per command), unknown SKU (history/receive/ship), bad quantity (anything not `[0-9]+` with value >= 1, e.g. `-5`, `+5`, `0`, `abc`), a note containing `\n` or `\r`, a movement that would make stock negative at any point in date order, unknown order (quote/fulfil/invoice), fulfil DATE before the order date, invoice with nothing shipped.
- On error: message on stderr prefixed `stockroom: `, naming file and line where there is one; nothing on stdout (build output in memory, write at the end).
- receive/ship: validate by re-parsing the existing movements plus the candidate line; append atomically-ish (read original bytes, add `\n` first if non-empty and not ending in `\n`, then the line + `\n`); create the file if missing. The printed/written line is `DATE SKU ±QTY[ NOTE]` with SKU upper-case. fulfil appends the same way.
- Output: single spaces; amounts with 2 decimals; discount `-7.50` or `0.00`. JSON via `json.dumps(..., indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)` with key orders as in the brief. Report text row: `SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme partial 10/15 177.27 148.20`; report sorted by (date, order id string). CSV via `csv` module with `\n` line terminator, header `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`.
- BrokenPipeError on stdout: exit 0 quietly (redirect stdout to devnull before exiting to avoid the interpreter's flush error).

**Build order.** Shelves half first (packaging + parsing + stock/low/history/receive/ship), orders half second (it depends on the shelves parsing). Split into issues as the decomposer sees fit; the two halves must be sequenced.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests use stdlib `unittest` (runnable via `python -m unittest` and pytest), in `tests/`. Test external behaviour: library functions on literal text, and the CLI via `subprocess` (`python -m stockroom`) in temp directories, asserting stdout, stderr content (file name + `line N`) and exit codes.
- Cover: every field rule's accept/reject cases from the brief; BOM, CRLF, lone CR, comment/blank lines and line numbering; negative-stock detection across out-of-order dates; the brief's worked `stock` and `quote` examples exactly; rounding half-up; order discount allocation with leftover pennies and ties; fulfil against later movements; invoice/report after partial shipment; receive/ship refusals leave the file byte-identical; newline added when missing; exit 2 cases; `stock | head -1` exits 0.
- A final check that `pip install .` into a fresh venv gives a working `stockroom` command and `import stockroom`.

## Out of Scope

- Third-party packages, any GUI/web interface, editing the catalogue or orders from the CLI, currencies other than GBP, concurrency/locking on the data files, Python < 3.9.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pip install .` installs the importable `stockroom` package and the `stockroom` console command; no third-party runtime dependencies; works on Python 3.9+.
- [ ] `parse_catalog`, `parse_movements`, `parse_orders`, `stock_levels`, `price_order`, `ParseError` are importable from `stockroom` with the attributes and types the brief specifies.
- [ ] `ParseError` is a `ValueError` with `.line`, message mentions `line N`; raised for every rule violation in the brief, with physical line numbers (blank/comment lines counted).
- [ ] BOM ignored; lines split only at LF/CRLF; blank and `#` comment lines ignored in all three files.
- [ ] Catalogue rules: SKU format and upper-casing, duplicate SKU, non-empty name, price format and minimum, reorder, optional tax field (4 or 5 fields), tax case-insensitive.
- [ ] Movement rules: valid date, known SKU (any case), non-zero signed quantity, note preserved trimmed; the line that first takes stock below zero in date order (stable within a day) is reported.
- [ ] Order rules: `SO-` id (any case, upper-cased, leading zeros significant, unique), valid date, one-word customer, `SKU*QTY` lines with known SKU once per order and qty >= 1.
- [ ] `stock` and `stock --json` output exactly as specified (example in the brief reproduces exactly).
- [ ] `low` and `low --json`, with BUY = `max(1, 2*reorder - onhand)`.
- [ ] `history SKU` and `--json` (delta as signed string), in counting order, note omitted when empty; unknown SKU refused (exit 1).
- [ ] `receive` / `ship` append `DATE SKU ±QTY[ NOTE]`, create the file if missing, add a missing final newline first, print the line; refusals (unknown SKU, bad quantity, negative stock at any point, note with line break) exit 1 and leave the file byte-identical; dash-led quantity is refused, dash-led note is a note.
- [ ] `price_order` implements steps 1-6 exactly with half-up rounding, largest-remainder allocation of the order discount (ties to earlier line), per-line tax; all amounts 2-dp Decimals; discounts <= 0.
- [ ] `quote ORDER` and `--json` reproduce the brief's example exactly; unknown order refused.
- [ ] `fulfil ORDER DATE` ships min(owed, available) where available respects later movements, appends `DATE SKU -N order SO-X` lines, prints per-line shipped/backordered and status open/partial/complete; DATE before order date refused.
- [ ] `invoice ORDER` and `--json` price the shipped quantities with the `invoice ` header prefix; nothing shipped is refused.
- [ ] `report` with `--format text|csv|json` (text default), sorted by date then order id, columns and types as specified.
- [ ] Each command reads only the files it needs; missing `movements.txt`/`orders.txt` are empty; missing `catalog.txt` exits 2.
- [ ] `--dir DIR` accepted anywhere on the line; options spelled in full only.
- [ ] Exit codes: 0 success; 1 data mistake or refusal (stderr names file and line, stdout empty); 2 unreadable file / missing dir / non-UTF-8 / command-line error (no/unknown command, wrong arg count, unknown option, bad option value, mistyped date).
- [ ] Broken pipe on stdout exits 0 quietly.
- [ ] A `unittest` suite in `tests/` covers the above and passes.

## Original request

# Stockroom

I run a small online shop out of a spare room and I keep everything in plain text files: what I sell,
what came in and went out of the shelves, and what customers ordered. I'd like a Python tool called
**stockroom** that reads those files and answers three questions: what is on the shelves and what
needs buying, what an order costs, and what I can ship today. It should work two ways: as a library I
can `import stockroom` from my own scripts, and as a `stockroom` command in the terminal. Python 3.9 or
newer, standard library only (no third-party packages). Running `pip install .` in the project folder
should give me both the importable library and the `stockroom` command.

There are two halves to it: the **shelves** (the catalogue, the stock movements, what is low) and the
**orders** (prices, discounts, tax, shipping what is in stock, invoices, a report). The orders half
depends on the shelves, so build them in that order.

## The three files

They live in one folder (the command's current folder, or the one named by `--dir`). Text is UTF-8; a
byte order mark at the start of a file is ignored; a line ends at LF or at CRLF and nowhere else.
In every file, blank lines are ignored, and so are lines starting with `#` (after any leading
whitespace). Anything else that does not follow the rules below is a mistake in my file, and the tool
must tell me which file and which line (counting from 1, blank and comment lines included).

### `catalog.txt` — what I sell

One product per line, fields separated by `|`, whitespace around each field trimmed:

```
# SKU   | name            | price | reorder | tax
AB-100 | Garden gnome     | 12.50 | 5       | standard
cd-205 | Seed packet, mix | 1.99  | 40      | reduced
EF-310 | Gift voucher     | 25.00 | 0
```

- **SKU**: two to four letters, a dash, three digits (`AB-100`). Letters in any case are accepted; the
  SKU is always shown in upper case. Two lines with the same SKU are a mistake.
- **name**: not empty. It may contain anything except `|`.
- **price**: in pounds, at least `0.01`, at most two decimal places (`12`, `12.5`, `1.99` are fine;
  `12.505`, `1,000.00`, `-3` and `abc` are not).
- **reorder**: the stock level at or under which I need to buy more: a whole number, zero or more.
- **tax** (optional, `standard` when the field is left out, so a line has four or five fields): one of
  `standard` (20 %), `reduced` (5 %) or `zero` (0 %), in any case.

### `movements.txt` — what came in and went out

One movement per line: `DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]`, separated by any amount of spaces or tabs. The note
is the rest of the line exactly as written, apart from trimming whitespace at both ends.

```
2024-03-01 AB-100 +20 first delivery
2024-03-04 ab-100 -3 order SO-1001
2024-03-05 CD-205 40
```

- **DATE** is `YYYY-MM-DD` and a date that exists (`2024-02-30` is a mistake).
- **SKU** must be in the catalogue (any case).
- **QUANTITY** is a whole number that is not zero, with an optional sign: positive means stock in,
  negative means stock out.
- The movements count in date order; movements on the same day keep the order of the file. The
  stock of a product may never be below zero at any point in that order. The line that takes it below
  zero is the mistake.

### `orders.txt` — what customers ordered

One order per line: `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER LINES`, separated by any amount of spaces or tabs:

```
SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme AB-100*12,CD-205*3
SO-1002 2024-03-09 Bea ab-100*2
```

- **ORDER** is `SO-` (any case) and one or more digits, shown in upper case; `SO-7` and `SO-007` are two
  different orders. It is unique: a second line with the same order number is a mistake.
- **DATE** as above. **CUSTOMER** is one word, shown as typed.
- **LINES** is one or more `SKU*QUANTITY` pairs separated by commas, no spaces. The SKU must be in the
  catalogue and appear once per order; the quantity is a whole number of one or more (no sign).

A missing `catalog.txt` is an error for every command. A missing `movements.txt` or `orders.txt` is
just empty. A command reads only the files it needs, and a mistake in a file it does not read is not its
business: the shelves commands (`stock`, `low`, `history`, `receive`, `ship`) read the catalogue and the
movements; `quote` reads the catalogue and the orders; `fulfil`, `invoice` and `report` read all three.

## Using it as a library

```python
import stockroom

catalog = stockroom.parse_catalog(open("catalog.txt").read())
moves = stockroom.parse_movements(open("movements.txt").read(), catalog)
print(stockroom.stock_levels(catalog, moves))
```

- `parse_catalog(text)` returns a `dict` of SKU to a product. A product has `.sku`, `.name`, `.price`
  (a `decimal.Decimal`), `.reorder` (an `int`) and `.tax` (`"standard"`, `"reduced"` or `"zero"`).
- `parse_movements(text, catalog)` returns a list of movements in the order they appear in the text,
  each with `.date` (a `datetime.date`), `.sku`, `.quantity` (an `int`) and `.note` (a `str`, empty when
  there is none).
- `parse_orders(text, catalog)` returns a list of orders in the order they appear, each with `.id`,
  `.date`, `.customer` and `.lines`: a list of `(sku, quantity)` pairs in the order written.
- A bad line makes any of these raise `stockroom.ParseError`. It is a `ValueError`, its `.line`
  attribute is the line number, and its message mentions `line N`.
- `stock_levels(catalog, movements)` is a `dict` of SKU to the quantity on the shelf, for every product
  in the catalogue (zero when it never moved).
- `price_order(order, catalog)` prices a whole order as described under *Prices* and returns a quote with
  `.lines` (each with `.sku`, `.quantity`, `.unit`, `.gross`, `.discount`, `.net`), `.subtotal`,
  `.order_discount`, `.tax` and `.total`, all `Decimal`s with two decimal places. A discount is zero or
  negative.

## Prices

All of this is exact to the penny and every rounding step rounds halves **up** (`0.005` becomes `0.01`).

1. A line's **gross** is its quantity times the unit price.
2. A line gets a **volume discount** of 5 % of its gross when the quantity is 10 or more, and 10 % when it
   is 50 or more (not both), rounded to the penny. The line's **net** is gross minus that.
3. The **subtotal** is the sum of the nets. When it is £500.00 or more the whole order gets an **order
   discount** of 3 % of the subtotal, rounded to the penny.
4. The order discount is shared out over the lines in proportion to their nets, to the penny: each line's
   share is rounded down, and the pennies left over go one each to the lines with the biggest part of a
   penny lost (the earlier line first on a tie). A line's **taxable amount** is its net less its share.
5. **Tax** is worked out per line on its taxable amount at its product's rate, rounded to the penny, and
   added up. Prices do not include tax.
6. The **total** is the subtotal, plus the order discount (a negative number), plus the tax.

AB-100 17 ok Garden gnome
CD-205 40 low Seed packet, mix
EF-310 0 out Gift voucher

order discount 0.00
tax 28.80
total 177.27

  line as `DATE DELTA BALANCE NOTE`: the quantity with its sign (`+20`, `-3`), the stock after the
  movement, and the note (and its space) left out when there is none. A SKU that is not in the catalogue is
  refused.
- `stockroom receive DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` and `stockroom ship DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` add a stock-in or
  stock-out movement to the end of `movements.txt` (creating it if needed) and print the line they added,
  written the way `history` writes a movement without the balance: `DATE SKU ±QUANTITY NOTE`. The quantity is a
  whole number of one or more, no sign. I pass the note as a single quoted argument; a note may not contain a
  line break. A movement that would break a rule above (an unknown SKU, a quantity that is not a positive
  whole number, stock that would go below zero at any point in date order) is refused and the file is left
  exactly as it was. If the file does not end in a newline, one is added before the new line.

  `subtotal`, `order discount`, `tax` and `total` lines. Amounts have two decimals, discounts carry a minus
  sign (zero has none), values are separated by single spaces. An order that is not in `orders.txt` is
  refused.

  quantity less what earlier shipments of this order sent (the total of the negative quantities for that SKU in movements
  whose note is exactly `order SO-1001`, the order number in upper case; capped at the quantity ordered). It ships as many of those as the shelves allow on

EF-310 | Gift voucher     | 25.00 | 0

6. The **total** is the subtotal, plus the order discount (a negative number), plus the tax.

## Using it from the terminal

Every command takes `--dir DIR` anywhere on the line (default: the current folder). Options are spelled out in full.

```
$ stockroom stock
AB-100 17 ok Garden gnome
CD-205 40 low Seed packet, mix
EF-310 0 out Gift voucher

$ stockroom quote SO-1001
SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme
AB-100 12 12.50 150.00 -7.50 142.50
CD-205 3 1.99 5.97 0.00 5.97
subtotal 148.47
order discount 0.00
tax 28.80
total 177.27
```

**The shelves**

- `stockroom stock [--json]` prints one line per product, by SKU: `SKU ONHAND STATUS NAME` separated by single
  spaces. The status is `out` when the stock is zero, `low` when it is above zero and at or under the product's
  reorder level, `ok` otherwise.
- `stockroom low [--json]` prints one line for each product that is `low` or `out`, by SKU:
  `SKU ONHAND REORDER BUY` where BUY is how many to buy to get back to twice the reorder level, and at least 1
  (`max(1, 2 × reorder − onhand)`).
- `stockroom history SKU [--json]` prints that product's movements, in the order they count, one per
  line as `DATE DELTA BALANCE NOTE`: the quantity with its sign (`+20`, `-3`), the stock after the
  movement, and the note (and its space) left out when there is none. A SKU that is not in the catalogue is
  refused.
- `stockroom receive DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` and `stockroom ship DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` add a stock-in or
  stock-out movement to the end of `movements.txt` (creating it if needed) and print the line they added,
  written the way `history` writes a movement without the balance: `DATE SKU ±QUANTITY NOTE`. The quantity is a
  whole number of one or more, no sign. I pass the note as a single quoted argument; a note may not contain a
  line break. A movement that would break a rule above (an unknown SKU, a quantity that is not a positive
  whole number, stock that would go below zero at any point in date order) is refused and the file is left
  exactly as it was. If the file does not end in a newline, one is added before the new line.

**The orders**

- `stockroom quote ORDER [--json]` prints the order priced as in the example: a header line
  `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER`, one line per order line `SKU QUANTITY UNIT GROSS DISCOUNT NET`, then
  `subtotal`, `order discount`, `tax` and `total` lines. Amounts have two decimals, discounts carry a minus
  sign (zero has none), values are separated by single spaces. An order that is not in `orders.txt` is
  refused.
- `stockroom fulfil ORDER DATE` ships what the shelves can cover. For each order line, what is still owed is its
  quantity less what earlier shipments of this order sent (the total of the negative quantities for that SKU in movements
  whose note is exactly `order SO-1001`, the order number in upper case; capped at the quantity ordered). It ships as many of those as the shelves allow on
  DATE: no more than the stock after all movements dated on or before DATE, and no more than the lowest stock at
  any later point (so that the shipment never makes a later movement take the stock below zero). It adds one
  movement `DATE SKU -N order SO-1001` per line with something to ship, at the end of the file. It prints one
  line per order line, `SKU shipped N backordered M` (M is what is still owed afterwards), then
  `status open`, `status partial` or `status complete`: `complete` when nothing is owed on any line, `open` when
  nothing has been shipped on any line yet, `partial` otherwise. DATE may not be before the order's date
  (refused).
- `stockroom invoice ORDER [--json]` is `quote` for what has actually shipped: the same rules and the same
  layout, with the quantities shipped so far (lines with nothing shipped are left out) and `invoice ` in front
  of the header line (`invoice SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme`). An order with nothing shipped is refused.
- `stockroom report [--format text|csv|json]` has one row per order, by order date and then by order
  number: `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER STATUS SHIPPED/ORDERED QUOTED INVOICED`: the status as above, the units shipped and
  ordered, the quote's total, and the invoice's total (`0.00` when nothing has shipped). `text` is the
  default and separates by single spaces. `csv` has the header
  `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`; `json` is an array of objects with those keys,
  the units as numbers and the amounts as strings with two decimals.
- With `--json`, `stock` prints an array of `{"sku", "name", "onhand", "status"}`, `low` an array of
  `{"sku", "onhand", "reorder", "buy"}`, `history` an array of `{"date", "delta", "balance", "note"}`, and
  `quote` / `invoice` an object with `order`, `date`, `customer`, `lines` (objects with `sku`, `quantity`,
  `unit`, `gross`, `discount`, `net`), `subtotal`, `order_discount`, `tax` and `total`. Amounts are strings
  with two decimals, counts are numbers, except a history `delta`, which is the signed string (`"+20"`, `"-3"`).
- `receive`, `ship` and `fulfil` take no options except `--dir`: every other argument is taken as typed, so a
  dash-led quantity is a bad quantity (refused) and a dash-led note is a note.
- The command line is checked first (exit `2` for anything wrong with it), then the files are read, then the
  request is carried out.
- Exit status: `0` when it worked; `1` when a data file has a mistake or what I asked for is refused (an unknown
  SKU or order, a movement that would break a rule, nothing shipped yet), with a message on standard error that
  names the file and the line where there is one, and nothing on standard output; `2` when a file cannot be read
  (a missing `catalog.txt`, a folder that does not exist, bytes that are not UTF-8) or the command line is wrong
  (no command, an unknown command, the wrong number of arguments, an unknown option, a bad option value, a date I
  mistyped).
- If whatever is reading the output goes away (`stockroom stock | head -1`) it just stops quietly, with status
  `0`.

"""Parsers for catalog.txt, movements.txt and orders.txt, plus stock levels."""

import datetime
import re
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Dict, Iterable, Iterator, List, Tuple

from .models import Movement, Order, Product

WS = " \t"
TAX_RATES = {"standard": Decimal("0.20"), "reduced": Decimal("0.05"), "zero": Decimal("0")}

SKU_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3}")
PRICE_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,2})?")
COUNT_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9]+")
SIGNED_RE = re.compile(r"[+-]?[0-9]+")
DATE_RE = re.compile(r"([0-9]{4})-([0-9]{2})-([0-9]{2})")
ORDER_ID_RE = re.compile(r"[Ss][Oo]-[0-9]+")
ORDER_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"([A-Za-z]{2,4}-[0-9]{3})\*([0-9]+)")
SEP_RE = re.compile(r"[ \t]+")

PENNY = Decimal("0.01")


class ParseError(ValueError):
    """A mistake in a data file. ``.line`` is the 1-based physical line number."""

    def __init__(self, line: int, reason: str):
        self.line = line
        self.reason = reason
        super().__init__("line %d: %s" % (line, reason))


def split_lines(text: str) -> List[str]:
    """Split text at LF or CRLF only, after dropping a leading byte order mark."""
    if text.startswith("﻿"):
        text = text[1:]
    lines = text.split("\n")
    return [ln[:-1] if ln.endswith("\r") else ln for ln in lines]


def content_lines(text: str) -> Iterator[Tuple[int, str]]:
    """Yield (line number, line) for every line that is neither blank nor a comment."""
    for number, line in enumerate(split_lines(text), start=1):
        stripped = line.strip(WS)
        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
            continue
        yield number, line


def parse_date(value: str):
    """Return a datetime.date for a YYYY-MM-DD string naming a real day, else None."""
    m = DATE_RE.fullmatch(value)
    if not m:
        return None
    try:
        return datetime.date(int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)))
    except ValueError:
        return None


def is_sku(value: str) -> bool:
    return SKU_RE.fullmatch(value) is not None


def parse_catalog(text: str) -> Dict[str, Product]:
    """Parse catalog.txt text into a dict of upper-case SKU to Product."""
    catalog: Dict[str, Product] = {}
    for number, line in content_lines(text):
        fields = [f.strip(WS) for f in line.split("|")]
        if len(fields) not in (4, 5):
            raise ParseError(number, "expected 4 or 5 fields separated by '|', found %d" % len(fields))
        sku, name, price, reorder = fields[:4]
        if not is_sku(sku):
            raise ParseError(number, "bad SKU %r" % sku)
        sku = sku.upper()
        if sku in catalog:
            raise ParseError(number, "duplicate SKU %s" % sku)
        if not name:
            raise ParseError(number, "empty name")
        if not PRICE_RE.fullmatch(price):
            raise ParseError(number, "bad price %r" % price)
        amount = Decimal(price).quantize(PENNY)
        if amount < PENNY:
            raise ParseError(number, "bad price %r (must be at least 0.01)" % price)
        if not COUNT_RE.fullmatch(reorder):
            raise ParseError(number, "bad reorder level %r" % reorder)
        tax = "standard"
        if len(fields) == 5:
            tax = fields[4].lower()
            if tax not in TAX_RATES:
                raise ParseError(number, "bad tax %r" % fields[4])
        catalog[sku] = Product(sku=sku, name=name, price=amount, reorder=int(reorder), tax=tax)
    return catalog


def counting_order(movements: Iterable[Movement]) -> List[Movement]:
    """Movements in the order they count: by date, file order within a day."""
    return sorted(movements, key=lambda m: m.date)


def parse_movements(text: str, catalog) -> List[Movement]:
    """Parse movements.txt text. Returns movements in text order.

    Raises ParseError for a malformed line, and for the first line (in counting
    order) that takes a product's stock below zero.
    """
    entries: List[Tuple[int, Movement]] = []
    for number, line in content_lines(text):
        parts = SEP_RE.split(line.strip(WS), maxsplit=3)
        if len(parts) < 3:
            raise ParseError(number, "expected DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]")
        date_s, sku, qty_s = parts[:3]
        note = parts[3].strip(WS) if len(parts) == 4 else ""
        date = parse_date(date_s)
        if date is None:
            raise ParseError(number, "bad date %r" % date_s)
        if not is_sku(sku):
            raise ParseError(number, "bad SKU %r" % sku)
        sku = sku.upper()
        if sku not in catalog:
            raise ParseError(number, "unknown SKU %s" % sku)
        if not SIGNED_RE.fullmatch(qty_s) or int(qty_s) == 0:
            raise ParseError(number, "bad quantity %r" % qty_s)
        entries.append((number, Movement(date=date, sku=sku, quantity=int(qty_s), note=note)))

    balance: Dict[str, int] = {}
    for number, mv in sorted(entries, key=lambda e: e[1].date):
        balance[mv.sku] = balance.get(mv.sku, 0) + mv.quantity
        if balance[mv.sku] < 0:
            raise ParseError(
                number, "stock of %s goes below zero (%d) on %s" % (mv.sku, balance[mv.sku], mv.date.isoformat())
            )
    return [mv for _, mv in entries]


def parse_orders(text: str, catalog) -> List[Order]:
    """Parse orders.txt text. Returns orders in text order."""
    orders: List[Order] = []
    seen = set()
    for number, line in content_lines(text):
        parts = SEP_RE.split(line.strip(WS))
        if len(parts) != 4:
            raise ParseError(number, "expected ORDER DATE CUSTOMER LINES")
        oid, date_s, customer, lines_s = parts
        if not ORDER_ID_RE.fullmatch(oid):
            raise ParseError(number, "bad order number %r" % oid)
        oid = oid.upper()
        if oid in seen:
            raise ParseError(number, "duplicate order %s" % oid)
        date = parse_date(date_s)
        if date is None:
            raise ParseError(number, "bad date %r" % date_s)
        lines: List[Tuple[str, int]] = []
        skus = set()
        for part in lines_s.split(","):
            m = ORDER_LINE_RE.fullmatch(part)
            if not m:
                raise ParseError(number, "bad order line %r" % part)
            sku, qty = m.group(1).upper(), int(m.group(2))
            if qty < 1:
                raise ParseError(number, "bad quantity in %r" % part)
            if sku not in catalog:
                raise ParseError(number, "unknown SKU %s" % sku)
            if sku in skus:
                raise ParseError(number, "SKU %s appears twice in order %s" % (sku, oid))
            skus.add(sku)
            lines.append((sku, qty))
        seen.add(oid)
        orders.append(Order(id=oid, date=date, customer=customer, lines=lines))
    return orders


def stock_levels(catalog, movements) -> Dict[str, int]:
    """Quantity on the shelf for every product in the catalogue."""
    levels = {sku: 0 for sku in catalog}
    for mv in movements:
        levels[mv.sku] = levels.get(mv.sku, 0) + mv.quantity
    return levels
"""Exact-to-the-penny order pricing."""

from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

from .models import Quote, QuoteLine
from .parsing import TAX_RATES

PENNY = Decimal("0.01")
ZERO = Decimal("0.00")
ORDER_DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD = Decimal("500.00")
ORDER_DISCOUNT_RATE = Decimal("0.03")


def round_penny(value: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """Round to two places, halves up; never returns negative zero."""
    result = value.quantize(PENNY, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return result if result != 0 else ZERO


def volume_rate(quantity: int) -> Decimal:
    if quantity >= 50:
        return Decimal("0.10")
    if quantity >= 10:
        return Decimal("0.05")
    return Decimal("0")


def allocate(total_pennies: int, weights):
    """Share total_pennies over weights (integers) by largest remainder.

    Each share is rounded down; leftover pennies go one each to the biggest
    fractional remainders, the earlier index first on a tie.
    """
    denominator = sum(weights)
    if total_pennies == 0 or denominator == 0:
        return [0] * len(weights)
    shares = []
    remainders = []
    for w in weights:
        q, r = divmod(total_pennies * w, denominator)
        shares.append(q)
        remainders.append(r)
    leftover = total_pennies - sum(shares)
    for i in sorted(range(len(weights)), key=lambda i: (-remainders[i], i))[:leftover]:
        shares[i] += 1
    return shares


def price_order(order, catalog) -> Quote:
    """Price an object with ``.lines`` of (sku, quantity) pairs against a catalogue."""
    lines = []
    for sku, quantity in order.lines:
        product = catalog[sku.upper()]
        unit = round_penny(product.price)
        gross = round_penny(unit * quantity)
        volume = round_penny(gross * volume_rate(quantity))
        net = round_penny(gross - volume)
        lines.append(QuoteLine(sku=product.sku, quantity=quantity, unit=unit, gross=gross,
                               discount=round_penny(-volume), net=net))

    subtotal = round_penny(sum((ln.net for ln in lines), ZERO))
    discount = ZERO
    if subtotal >= ORDER_DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD:
        discount = round_penny(subtotal * ORDER_DISCOUNT_RATE)

    shares = allocate(int(discount * 100), [int(ln.net * 100) for ln in lines])
    tax = ZERO
    for ln, share in zip(lines, shares):
        taxable = ln.net - Decimal(share) / 100
        rate = TAX_RATES[catalog[ln.sku].tax]
        tax += round_penny(taxable * rate)
    tax = round_penny(tax)

    return Quote(lines=lines, subtotal=subtotal, order_discount=round_penny(-discount),
                 tax=tax, total=round_penny(subtotal - discount + tax))
"""stockroom: inventory and order tool for a small shop, driven by plain text files."""

from .models import Movement, Order, Product, Quote, QuoteLine
from .parsing import ParseError, parse_catalog, parse_movements, parse_orders, stock_levels
from .pricing import price_order

__all__ = [
    "Movement",
    "Order",
    "ParseError",
    "Product",
    "Quote",
    "QuoteLine",
    "parse_catalog",
    "parse_movements",
    "parse_orders",
    "price_order",
    "stock_levels",
]

__version__ = "0.1.0"
import sys

from .cli import main

sys.exit(main())

            if sku not in catalog:

def stock_levels(catalog, movements) -> Dict[str, int]:
    """Quantity on the shelf for every product in the catalogue."""
    levels = {sku: 0 for sku in catalog}
    for mv in movements:
        levels[mv.sku] = levels.get(mv.sku, 0) + mv.quantity
    return levels
"""Exact-to-the-penny order pricing."""

from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

from .models import Quote, QuoteLine
from .parsing import TAX_RATES

PENNY = Decimal("0.01")
ZERO = Decimal("0.00")
ORDER_DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD = Decimal("500.00")
ORDER_DISCOUNT_RATE = Decimal("0.03")


def round_penny(value: Decimal) -> Decimal:
    """Round to two places, halves up; never returns negative zero."""
    result = value.quantize(PENNY, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return result if result != 0 else ZERO


def volume_rate(quantity: int) -> Decimal:
    if quantity >= 50:
        return Decimal("0.10")
    if quantity >= 10:
        return Decimal("0.05")
    return Decimal("0")


def allocate(total_pennies: int, weights):
    """Share total_pennies over weights (integers) by largest remainder.

    Each share is rounded down; leftover pennies go one each to the biggest
    fractional remainders, the earlier index first on a tie.
    """
    denominator = sum(weights)
    if total_pennies == 0 or denominator == 0:
        return [0] * len(weights)
    shares = []
    remainders = []
    for w in weights:
        q, r = divmod(total_pennies * w, denominator)
        shares.append(q)
        remainders.append(r)
    leftover = total_pennies - sum(shares)
    for i in sorted(range(len(weights)), key=lambda i: (-remainders[i], i))[:leftover]:
        shares[i] += 1
    return shares


def price_order(order, catalog) -> Quote:
    """Price an object with ``.lines`` of (sku, quantity) pairs against a catalogue."""
    lines = []
    for sku, quantity in order.lines:
        product = catalog[sku.upper()]
        unit = round_penny(product.price)
        gross = round_penny(unit * quantity)
        volume = round_penny(gross * volume_rate(quantity))
        net = round_penny(gross - volume)
        lines.append(QuoteLine(sku=product.sku, quantity=quantity, unit=unit, gross=gross,
                               discount=round_penny(-volume), net=net))

    subtotal = round_penny(sum((ln.net for ln in lines), ZERO))
    discount = ZERO
    if subtotal >= ORDER_DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD:
        discount = round_penny(subtotal * ORDER_DISCOUNT_RATE)

    shares = allocate(int(discount * 100), [int(ln.net * 100) for ln in lines])
    tax = ZERO
    for ln, share in zip(lines, shares):
        taxable = ln.net - Decimal(share) / 100
        rate = TAX_RATES[catalog[ln.sku].tax]
        tax += round_penny(taxable * rate)
    tax = round_penny(tax)

    return Quote(lines=lines, subtotal=subtotal, order_discount=round_penny(-discount),
                 tax=tax, total=round_penny(subtotal - discount + tax))

    57	class Failure(Exception):

    73	def parse_args(argv):
    74	    """Return (command, positionals, options dict). Raises Failure(2) on any problem."""
    75	    directory = "."
    76	    rest = []
    77	    i = 0
    78	    while i < len(argv):
    79	        arg = argv[i]
    80	        if arg == "--dir":
    81	            if i + 1 >= len(argv):
    82	                raise usage_error("option --dir needs a value")
    83	            directory = argv[i + 1]
    84	            i += 2
    85	            continue
    86	        if arg.startswith("--dir="):
    87	            directory = arg[len("--dir="):]
    88	            i += 1
    89	            continue
    90	        rest.append(arg)
    91	        i += 1
    92	    if directory == "":
    93	        raise usage_error("option --dir needs a value")
    94	
    95	    # The command is the first argument that is not an option (or an option's value).
    96	    command_at = None
    97	    j = 0
    98	    while j < len(rest):
    99	        if rest[j] == "--format":
   100	            j += 2
   101	            continue
   102	        if not is_option(rest[j]):
   103	            command_at = j
   104	            break
   105	        j += 1
   106	    if command_at is None:
   107	        if rest:
   108	            raise usage_error("no command (unknown option %r?)" % rest[0])
   109	        raise usage_error("no command given")
   110	    command = rest[command_at]
   111	    if command not in COMMANDS:
   112	        raise usage_error("unknown command %r" % command)
   113	    others = rest[:command_at] + rest[command_at + 1:]
   114	    counts, allowed = COMMANDS[command]
   115	
   116	    options = {"dir": directory, "json": False, "format": "text"}
   117	    positionals = []
   118	    if command in RAW_COMMANDS:
   119	        positionals = others
   120	    else:
   121	        k = 0
   122	        while k < len(others):
   123	            arg = others[k]
   124	            if not is_option(arg):
   125	                positionals.append(arg)
   126	            elif arg == "--json" and "--json" in allowed:
   127	                options["json"] = True
   128	            elif arg == "--format" and "--format" in allowed:
   129	                if k + 1 >= len(others):
   130	                    raise usage_error("option --format needs a value")
   131	                options["format"] = others[k + 1]
   132	                k += 1
   133	            elif arg.startswith("--format=") and "--format" in allowed:
   134	                options["format"] = arg[len("--format="):]
   135	            else:
   136	                raise usage_error("unknown option %r for %s" % (arg, command))
   137	            k += 1
   138	        if options["format"] not in FORMATS:
   139	            raise usage_error("bad --format value %r (use text, csv or json)" % options["format"])
   140	
   141	    if len(positionals) not in counts:
   142	        raise usage_error("wrong number of arguments for %s" % command)
   143	
   144	    if command in ("receive", "ship"):
   145	        check_date_arg(positionals[0])
   146	    elif command == "fulfil":

   163	def read_text(directory, name, required):

content.text:
I checked every criterion against the code and ran the probes against the real CLI. 20 of the 21 criteria are met and the probe list passes, but there is one unmet criterion and a few smaller issues. All 94 unittests pass. `pip install --target` (with a fresh `build/`) produced a working `stockroom` command; I couldn't do a full venv install because the machine has no `ensurepip`. Scratch data is in `/tmp/stockroom-probe-797000`; no tracked files were changed.

## Unmet criterion

1. **Exit codes and amounts for very large numbers.** These come out as tracebacks or wrong pennies instead of an error message.
   - **Huge integers (over 4300 digits).** A quantity or reorder level that long, in any file or in `receive`/`ship`, hits Python's int-conversion limit and raises `ValueError`. Repro: `receive 2024-03-10 AB-100 $(python3 -c "print('9'*5000)")`, or the same number in movements, catalogue reorder or order quantity. Expected: exit 1 with file and line (exit 1 refusal for the CLI argument). Actual: traceback, exit 1. A `ship`/`receive` refusal still leaves the file byte-identical.
   - **Amounts past 28 significant digits.** These raise `decimal.InvalidOperation` because the code runs at the default Decimal precision. Repro: catalogue `AB-100|x|99999999999999999999999999999.99|0` then `stock`, or an order `AB-100*1000000000000000000000000000` then `quote`. The library `parse_catalog` raises it too, not `ParseError`. Expected: `ParseError` / exit 1, or exact arithmetic. Actual: traceback.
   - **Wrong pennies above about £10^13.** `money()` in `src/stockroom/cli.py:233` uses `"%.2f" % value`, which turns the Decimal into a float. Repro: catalogue `AB-100|x|99999999999999.99|0`, order `AB-100*1000`, then `quote SO-1`. That prints unit `99999999999999.98` and gross `99999999999999984.00`; the correct values are `.99` and `99999999999999990.00`. Text and JSON output are both affected; the library's Decimals are correct. Fix: `format(value, ".2f")`.

## Other I/O issues

2. **Stdout closed (`>&-`).** `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m stockroom stock >&-` gives `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'` from `write_stream` (`cli.py:495`), exit 1. Expected: exit quietly. Writing to `/dev/full` gives exit 120 with `Exception ignored on flushing sys.stdout`.
3. **Lone CR at end of file is stripped.** `printf '2024-03-01 AB-100 +20\r' > movements.txt; stock` is accepted as `+20`. `split_lines` drops a final `\r` even with no LF after it. The brief says a line ends only at LF or CRLF, so this should be `bad quantity '+20\r'`, exit 1, as happens with `\r\r\n`.
4. **Refusal message gives no line number.** `ship 2024-03-02 AB-100 18` prints `refused: 2024-03-02 AB-100 -18: stock of AB-100 goes below zero (-1) on 2024-03-04`. The existing line that would go negative (movements.txt line 2) is in the error, but `exc.reason` drops it. This is a soft reading of "names the file and the line where there is one".
5. **Report order is a string sort (decision for you).** `report` sorts by date then order ID as text, so `SO-10` comes before `SO-9` and `SO-007` before `SO-7` on the same day. The PRD says string sort; the brief says "by order number". Worth confirming which is wanted.
6. **`ParseError` can't be pickled or copied** (minor, library). Its `__init__(line, reason)` breaks `pickle`/`copy`: `TypeError: missing 'reason'`.

## Robustness probe results (all pass)

- **Dash-led values:**
  - `history -x` gives exit 2 (unknown option).
  - `quote -` gives exit 1 (unknown order).
  - `--dir -x` and `--dir --json` give exit 2 (folder does not exist).
  - `--format -` gives exit 2.
  - `receive 2024-03-10 AB-100 -5` gives exit 1 (bad quantity).
  - `receive … 5 -note` and `receive … 5 --json` are taken as notes, exit 0.
  - `history --` gives exit 2.
  - `ship … --` gives exit 1.
  - `fulfil SO-1001 -x` gives exit 2 (bad date).
  - `--js`, `--json=1`, `--dir` with no value, `--dir=` and `--format CSV` all give exit 2.
- **Pipe into `head -1`:** `stock`, `stock --json`, `low`, `history`, `quote` and `report` (all three formats) all exit 0 with nothing on stderr. This holds for the brief's data and for a 20,000-product catalogue, and also when the reader closes immediately.
- **BOM, CRLF, non-UTF-8:** a BOM in each file is ignored, and CRLF is fine in each file. Non-UTF-8 bytes in each file give exit 2 naming the file.
- **Lone CR:** it never splits a line. An all-CR catalogue becomes one comment line, so the error shows up in movements as "unknown SKU". An all-CR movements file becomes one movement whose note contains the CRs. An all-CR orders file gives "line 1: expected ORDER DATE CUSTOMER LINES".
- **Form feed and U+2028:** they don't split lines and aren't trimmed as whitespace (a lone `\f` is a valid name or customer; `+1\f` is a bad quantity). They are printed raw in text, and JSON shows `\f` and a raw U+2028.
- **Missing folder or catalogue:** a missing folder, a missing `catalog.txt`, or a folder named `catalog.txt` or `movements.txt` gives exit 2. Empty files give empty output, `[]`, or just the CSV header.
- **Library:** `ParseError` subclasses `ValueError` with an `int` `.line` and a message containing `line N`. Field types are right, `.lines` is a list of tuples, and `price_order` works on a `SimpleNamespace(lines=…)` with lowercase SKUs.

## Criteria verified as met

- **Packaging:** installs, no dependencies, exports everything required.
- **Parsing:** every catalogue, movement and order field rule; line numbers counting blank and comment lines; the first line in date order that takes stock negative (stable within a day).
- **Shelves output:** `stock` (brief example exact), `low`, `history`.
- **`receive`/`ship`:** create the file if missing, add a missing final newline, refuse while leaving the file byte-identical, refuse notes with a line break.
- **Pricing steps 1–6:** half-up rounding (0.025 becomes 0.03), largest-remainder allocation with ties to the earlier line, tax per line, no `-0.00`.
- **Orders output:** `quote` (brief example exact, JSON too); `fulfil` respects later movements, caps at what's owed, writes nothing when nothing ships, and refuses a date before the order; `invoice`; `report` text/csv/json.
- **Command line and files:** each command reads only its own files; `--dir` and `--dir=` work anywhere; options must be spelled in full; the command line is checked before any file is read; stdout is empty on errors.
